entities.summary: Macarius Magnes, sometimes referred to as Macarius of Magnesia, is the author of a work of Christian apologetics contesting the writings of a Neo-Platonic philosopher. He was unknown for centuries until the discovery of a manuscript at Athens in 1867. This work is called Ἀποκριτικός πρὸς Ἕλληνας in Greek, and Apocriticus in Latin. It agrees in its dogmatics with Gregory of Nyssa, and is valuable on account of the numerous excerpts from the writings of the pagan opponent of Macarius. Macarius does not directly name the "Hellene" he is quoting from and criticizing, but it is most commonly speculated to be the philosopher Porphyry, who wrote a lost work called Against the Christians.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Macarius Magnes' work Apocriticus provides valuable insights into Neo-Platonic thought and Christian apologetics, shedding light on the intellectual debates of the late antique period. Its excerpts from Porphyry's lost work Against the Christians offer a unique window into the philosophical underpinnings of early Christianity.
